newsitem.title: USA: Bay State sees year net below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Bay State sees year net below estimates.

text.p: Bay State Gas Co said on Wednesday it expects its fiscal 1997 earnings will come in slightly lower than Wall Street analysts are forecasting.
The company cited warm weather, sluggish first quarter results, and development costs.
The consensus estimate for 1997 earnings is currently $2 a share, Bay State said, excluding the possibility of a sale of its MASSPOWER interest.
The company made the forecasts in comments accompanying its first quarter earnings announcement.

For the first fiscal quarter ended December 31, 1996, Bay State earned $0.98 a share, lower than the $1.07 it earned last year. It said weather, which was six percent warmer than last year, cut earnings per share by about $0.12.
The drop in profits from the warm weather was partially offset by the addition of more than 6,300 new customers in the past year, the company said, bringing its total to more than 300,000.
Bay State also expects revenues to grow sharply at its EnergyUSA affiliate and plans to invest in related purchases.

"We project EnergyUSA's revenues ... to grow significantly from last year's $17 million, with start-up and development costs incurred in fiscal 1997 ensuring earnings growth in fiscal 1998 and beyond," said Bay State's president and chief operating officer Joel Singer in the statement.

Bay State said it expects to file this week with the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities for authorization to invest up to an additional $50 million for acquisitions through either cash or common stock in EnergyUSA's area.
